direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is pretty standard for a college comedy; The direction on a microscale is where the comedy shines, as the chemistry within this friend/love triangle really makes this movie feel very awkward and pretty funny, like Crazy, Stupid, Love; The storytelling uses your investment in these characters and the awkward cringe to draw you in, as you want to see how things play out, with the ending unleashing this level of cringe and comedy that feels like that one scene from Crazy, Stupid, Love but stretched out for 40 minutes; Tension is built through its cringe as you crawl in your seat while watching how the story unfolds, with the final 40 minutes feeling like that one scene from Crazy, Stupid, Love

performance.comments: Plays her role well as you can really see her struggle to fit in as she doesn't feel at home in this new town and struggles to be a mother for her teenage daughter, having to build a relationship with these two college kids to try and find herself again; her chemistry with Feldman and Hoffman really brings this movie to life as they are all able to work off each other to make this movie feel fun

Plays this awkward character very well as this dude is now 3/3 in movies I've seen him play this type of character; his chemistry is good with the cast; he really steals the scenes he's in as he just feels like a natural, Im really happy this guy is getting more work cause he's a future star that can fill Michael Cera and Nathan Fielder's awkward void

Plays his role well as you can see him falling in love while also trying to grow and be an adult; really is the comedic character and plays it well, he really is his daddy's son :'); has good chemistry in the triangle

cast.comments: the movie is mainly about the love triangle, but their chemistry extends to the remaining cast as everyone plays their role well and helps move the story forward

story.comments: The concept is actually unique, as it follows two storylines converging in a college poetry class where Leslie Mann's character is trying to fit in as she escapes loneliness in a new place, and the college boys look to befriend her while they try to find out what they want in life (and try to bang her at the same time); The plot structure is like a kettle of boiling water, where the final 40 minutes is the lid coming off as madness ensues; The movie does have structural issues, though, because the film would have been much tighter if the filmmakers cut the exposition in half and completely cut out the resolution; Character writing is surprisingly good, as each character's motivations are clearly outlined and you see how each character learns from one another

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is pretty polished and well-written; The humor is definitely there, as it keeps the movie lighthearted and entertaining; The symbolism is somewhat present, as you learn a lot from these characters learning more about themselves as they open up to each other, taking flavors from many coming-of-age college movies; The foreshadowing is pretty standard and somewhat expected once you are 40 minutes in

score.comments: The score helps with setting the tone and tension

cinematography.comments: The cinematography feels surprisingly polished for an indie directorial debut, and I wonder how she got all these connections

editing.comments: The editing feels surprisingly polished for an indie directorial debut, and I wonder how she got all these connections

production_design.comments: The production design uses the college setting well, as it gives the movie a very Northeast campus in the fall vibe

review.pacing: Pacing is a major issue for this movie because the beginning and ending really drag; If you cut the exposition in half and completely cut out the resolution, you would save 30 minutes and have a much tighter movie
review.climax: The climax is very cringey and entertaining because it just feels like that one scene in Crazy, Stupid, Love but stretched out for 40 minutes
review.tone: The tone feels like a lighthearted comedy set in a college town, following a love triangle dynamic
review.final_notes: I saw the U.S. premiere at SXSW; This movie really is nepotism's final boss
review.overall: Overall, 'Poetic License' beats being nepotism's final boss by being a polished college comedy that is brought to life by the love triangle dynamic between Leslie Mann, Cooper Hoffman, and Andrew Barth Feldman, as the chemistry between the three makes this movie a fun watch and keeps you emotionally invested in this kettle-like story, especially when the lid comes off toward the end, as the final 40 minutes have the same cringey and chaotic feeling as that one scene from 'Crazy, Stupid, Love'; While it does have its strengths, the movie does feel a bit bloated and would have benefited from cutting the exposition in half and completely cutting out the resolution, as the movie would have saved 30 minutes and felt tighter
